review: Read-only source review of native scene app and local data packager
checked_contracts: World bootstrap remains stopped before presentation/dialogue opcode; app labels unfinished campaign controls.
Resource309 is 207 counted bytes; initial form0/action1 animation selection is checked against descriptor animations.
Atlas parser validates frame indices; animation constructor rejects empty/zero-duration sequences before indexed app use.
CPU SceneVertex32-byte/UVoffset16 and Uniform80-byte layouts match shader structs; column-major matrix multiplication is consistent.
PNG decoder returns straight RGBA; Metal uses matching source-alpha RGB and one/one-minus-source-alpha alpha blending.
ObjC++17 and ARC are set for renderer, app and probe; required frameworks are linked.
GPU/scene resource failures pause rendering; asynchronous completion/presentation callbacks use weak references and main-queue dispatch.
Presentation statistics use drawable presentedTime, with explicit recent-scene-only scope; elapsed milliseconds drive animation independently of frame count.
Packager bounds ZIP input and rejects unsafe/repeated/symlink/encrypted entries; only expected app members enter output.
Packager verifies thin native ARM64 Mach-O, iPhoneOS17.5, bundle identity, source-commit/executable-hash agreement and exact original-data hashes.
Only iphone.big and the verified480-byte terrain data tables are added; original Mach-O executable and compatibility runtime are not added.
Output ZIP re-read verifies inventory and byte equality; native executable mode755 is preserved in finalIPA.
limits: Inspection camera, culling/blending and whole-scene composition are not original-renderer parity claims.
No original-game full playthrough, campaign execution, native save/reload, audio/lifecycle acceptance or sustained iPhoneXR frame-rate validation is established by this review.
The code artifact is authenticated by expected commit/source-controlled CI context plus recorded hashes, not a cryptographic signature from this script.
Metal offscreen test uses synthetic pixels and reports unavailable devices as skipped; it is not iPhone gameplay evidence.
